hypothesis: Daily benchmark-relative return forecasts carry no stable IC, so pure return prediction cannot produce stable excess over SOXX. Test whether a bounded family of causal, non-leveraged exposure rules that use only past-available realized volatility and trend state can beat SOXX buy-and-hold on return, drawdown and Sharpe together, and whether any such rule holds on the newly available forward sessions.
parameter_search_budget: one pre-registered bounded family; no tuning after outcomes

state_definition.realized_vol: SOXX simple-return sample standard deviation over trailing 20 sessions, annualized by sqrt(252)
state_definition.trend: SOXX close versus trailing 200-session moving average
state_definition.causality: all state at signal close t is applied to session t+1 realized return; no look-ahead

allocation.trend_vol_switch: above trend and low vol -> (1,0,0); above trend and high vol -> (0,1,0); below trend -> (0,0,1)
allocation.fees: turnover * cost_bps charged on each rebalance; owned NAV, no reset

selection: development-only deterministic ranking by stable-excess satisfaction, then positive years, Sharpe difference and drawdown improvement; benchmark is never selectable

gates.stable_excess: beats SOXX return AND drawdown AND Sharpe on the window, with at least minimum_positive_years annual wins
gates.promotion: development AND reused_diagnostic stable excess at both 10bps and 25bps

stopping: Exactly the pre-registered family at two costs across three windows; no threshold, window or cost tuning after outcomes. Preserve all results, including failures.
limitations: Forward window is only the newly available sessions and is statistically weak.
No return forecast is used; this card isolates risk and trend structure only.
SOXL realized leverage decay is not modeled beyond its actual traded prices.
Diagnostic and forward windows never influence selection.
A negative result here does not refute mechanisms that use intraday state.
